items.title: Global FX Strategy: Warsh Unlikely to Reverse USD Selling Trends
items.summary: We don't think Fed Chair Warsh's remarks at Jackson Hole will reverse USD selling trends. Risks to this outcome are more around valuation and positioning, in our view, than fundamental reasons for a hawkish surprise. We offer further thoughts about directions Warsh could take in this note.

items.title: Off the Cuff: The TGA, Bank Reserves and Risky Assets
items.summary: Reports that the U.S. Treasury could use its general account to fund bond purchases have caught markets' attention. While there are no details about the size or scope, such a move would increase bank reserves, which could provide a boost to risky assets. We offer further analysis herein.

items.title: Metal Matters: We're Adjusting Our Gold Targets
items.summary: Gold breached our bullish 0-3 month point-price target of $4,500 an ounce following the U.S. Treasury announcement to increase long-end buybacks. We raise our 0-3 month target to $4,800 an ounce, as momentum has room to run, but keep our 6-12 month target unchanged at $5,000 an ounce.

items.title: Asia Shipping: The Return on Invested Capital Contenders
items.summary: In considering what's ahead for Asia's container shipping industry, we see Evergreen Marine, COSCO Shipping Holding and Wan Hai as the ROIC contenders that could deliver superior 2026-28 return on equity. We initiate coverage of Wan Hai and Regional Container Lines at Buy.

items.title: Our Takeaways From HD and LOW Earnings
items.summary: Earnings from Home Depot and Lowe's saw slight differences in performance, notably on same store sales. Both saw the benefit of tariff refunds to EPS, but also cited incremental cost pressures of higher freight/transportation and re-investment in customer-facing initiatives.

items.title: Africa Weekly: Policy Priorities Across Sub-Saharan Africa
items.summary: We consider the economic turnaround developing in Zimbabwe and then explore wider trends with respect to fiscal policies and debt dynamics that seem to be playing out across Sub-Saharan Africa.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence: Investing in Open Models
items.summary: The frontier intelligence available to the public remains unchanged. Labs hold back the general release of next-generation models, a pause partly explained by the launch of classified federal cyber reviews; we note that airtight containment and security lie beyond current model designs.

items.title: U.S. Rates Weekly: Can Bessent and Warsh Save the Curve?
items.summary: We got long 20y bonds after Treasury increased long-end buybacks. The long end now has better asymmetric risk-reward with the new Treasury “put” combined with attractive valuations, potential pension-fund demand, and upcoming softer data. We offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: Size & Style Chartbook: The Case for SMID Persists
items.summary: In this quarter’s Size & Style Chartbook, we note that the case for Small/Mid Cap exposure remains compelling despite year-to-date outperformance. But we also note that the style setup risks being misleading, while reflecting AI-related bottlenecks. We offer further takeaways herein.

items.title: U.S. Economics Weekly: The Resilience Narrative
items.summary: Recent increases in long-end yields were met with a surprise Treasury announcement doubling the size of debt buybacks, which ultimately did little to lower yields. We continue to think the Fed will return to rate cuts later this year in the face of softer employment and inflation data.

items.title: PULSE Monitor: Summer Conundrums
items.summary: Equity sentiment has turned more cautious, if not confused. Fundamentals remain solid, but reaction to Walmart results is a shot across the bow that consumer conviction remains suspect, further spotlighting the inflation/stagflation debate. Exit summer doldrums, enter summer conundrums?

items.title: European Equity Strategy: Unpacking Europe's Rebound
items.summary: European equities have been a key beneficiary of the "broadening trade." We remain Neutral on European equities in our global equity allocation, but observe that the longer-term case for holding Europe in global portfolios may be improving. We offer further details in this note.

items.title: Global Asset Allocation: House Views August 2026
items.summary: The U.S.-Iran conflict remains an overhang, mostly impacting fixed-income markets, though U.S. data have come in softer and Bessent has signaled his intent to stabilize the back end. We had been neutral duration, with an U.S. underweight against Europe, but are now revisiting that.

items.title: Walmart Faces a Multiple Issue, Not Multiple Issues
items.summary: Despite Walmart's recent stock decline, we think its core business remains healthy and it’s taking share across all income demographics. We see the stock pressure as more about having to fight the battle of having a high multiple in a market demanding perfection for high-multiple stocks.

items.title: Deep Dive: The Potential Impacts of Airline MRO Insourcing
items.summary: Airlines traditionally seen as reliable outsourcers are increasingly internalizing maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) capabilities. In this Deep Dive, we look at whether this shift could constitute a material threat to OEM aftermarket revenue, with Embraer as our primary focus.

items.title: Global Gas and Power Insights: Haynesville 2.0
items.summary: Many in the market could be underestimating Haynesville natural gas production, with upside surprises also expected from coming months' production. We analyze the production outlook and related developments — production, pipeline infrastructure and pricing — from the commodity angle.

items.title: Emerging Markets Strategy Weekly: Back-End USTs and EM Risk
items.summary: U.S. back-end rates are the epicenter of macro risk, driven by rising crude prices and fiscal concerns. If the U.S. Treasury's doubling of long-term debt purchases proves insufficient, depending on the equity response, we think EM risk may react to these developments in a heavier way.

items.title: Global Economic Outlook & Strategy: Still Just a Little Rain
items.summary: Two factors continue to shape the global outlook: First is the U.S.-Iran conflict, oil prices and associated uncertainties. Second is the global economy's still solid expansion despite these headwinds. All told, we see appreciable two-sided risks to both our growth and inflation forecasts.

items.title: Foreign Exchange Forecasts: August 2026
items.summary: We flip bearish USD and raise our EURUSD forecast to 1.1750 as hawkish Fed premium is priced out, relative data surprises favor Europe, and uncertainty around U.S. midterm elections enters our forecasting window. We offer further analysis and strategies in this note.

items.title: We're Downgrading TJX to Neutral
items.summary: We're downgrading TJX to Neutral. The second-quarter Marmaxx comp of +1% was weak and disappointing, a reminder that off-pricers aren't immune to fashion misses. We see a more balanced risk/reward as TJX tries to correct its execution issues within a tougher competitive landscape.

items.title: Lowe's Faces a Shift in Investor Focus Following Results
items.summary: Second-quarter results from Lowe's were positively received, but 2026 is essentially "de-risked" now. The thesis of LOW trailing HD on same store sales has largely played out; the focus now shifts to the overall housing/macro/rates backdrop, the key driver of upside for both stocks.

items.title: Target's Strategies Gain Traction But There's Still Work to Do
items.summary: Target's second consecutive quarter of positive comps shows management’s strategies are gaining traction. That said, market expectations are elevated and there remains risk that comp momentum isn't sustained. As discussed further in this note, we see a balanced risk/reward.

items.title: October Could Kick Off India's Rate-Hike Cycle
items.summary: Minutes from August's meeting and other media comments suggest India policymakers might consider rate hikes if inflation remains above 5%. We now see October as a "live" meeting for the start of the rate-hike cycle; our base case moves to 50-basis-point hikes starting in December.

items.title: The High-Grade Beat: The Path Forward for Hyperscalers
items.summary: Hyperscaler spreads have tightened, with renewed confidence in their trajectories given earnings clarity on capex and revenue generation. But further widening for hyperscaler spreads isn't out of the question, and the funding path going forward is likely to diversify further.

items.title: Our Take on the U.S. Treasury's Announcement: Buy Gold
items.summary: The U.S. Treasury's announcement to at least double long-end buybacks is a significant signal that should stabilize the back end of the curve and stall the momentum for higher yields. We are neutralizing our underweight on U.S. duration, and offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: Themes to Watch at Our Korea Investor Conference 2026
items.summary: We're hosting our Korea Investor Conference on Aug. 27–28, with 71 Korean and Japanese names holding meetings with investors. In this note, we highlight the key themes to watch for by sector, covering industry direction and outlook as well as investment ideas.

items.title: Oil Monitor: When Do We “Run Out” of Stockpiles?
items.summary: The U.S.-Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruptions have led to global observed inventory draws of ~3 million barrels a day. As an exercise, we project these forward, implying that OECD stockpiles could dwindle to ~70 days of cover as late as the end of 2027.

items.title: Global Commodities: Notes on Sugar, Cocoa and Coffee Trades
items.summary: We close our sugar call spread trade with a 58% profit. While our trade target of $1.20 remains achievable in principle, it may now prove too ambitious. We're also closing our Arabica coffee put call spread trade idea at a 40% loss. We offer further details in this note.

items.title: Brazil Diversified Banks: The Delinquency Paradox
items.summary: The paradox of Brazil's current cycle is simple: More credit, more transfers and more liquidity are no longer enough to prevent rising household financial stress. Delinquencies are rising despite a highly supportive backdrop — a cycle we expect to continue, as explored herein.

items.title: Brazil Elections: The Road to Planalto Palace 2026
items.summary: As we have officially entered Brazil's political campaign period, we present the first edition of our 2026 Presidential Elections Guide. We offer information about the political environment in Brazil, the main candidates' profiles, and a summary of voting intention polls.

items.title: U.S. Property & Casualty: Allstate Downgrade Feedback
items.summary: Response to our Allstate downgrade was balanced, but some pushback may reflect reluctance to sell a recent winner rather than a high-conviction bull case. We address five key debate points and expand our normalized framework comparing Progressive and Allstate.

items.title: Nvidia Earnings Preview: Focus on AI Financing
items.summary: Nvidia reports on August 26. We raise our sales estimates above the Street's and expect the stock to trade higher after earnings. We believe Nvidia has secured high-bandwidth memory supply and is now focused on addressing land, power, and shell bottlenecks to help expand AI factories.

items.title: Broadcom Earnings Preview: Focus on Updated 2027 AI Sales Outlook
items.summary: Broadcom reports on September 2. We model July quarter revenue/EPS modestly above consensus and July quarter modestly below. We keep our $116 bn FY27 AI revenue forecast and lift FY27/28 EPS on stronger software infrastructure sales growth. We maintain our Buy rating and $500 target price.

items.title: Japan FX: Our View of the U.S.-Japan Currency Alliance
items.summary: The first act of the U.S.-Japan “currency alliance” was U.S. Treasury intervention to sell EURJPY. We see a growing risk of Japanese MoF intervention if EURJPY reaches ¥185-186/€, while USDJPY remains the key battleground. Equity market conditions may influence timing.

items.title: The Speculative Grade Beat: Private Credit 2.0
items.summary: Nvidia’s plan to mobilize over $500 bn of third-party capital for AI infrastructure highlights private credit’s evolution beyond direct lending. This report maps the shift from Private Credit 1.0 and 1.5 toward a 2.0 model built around platform-scale capital solutions.

items.title: UK Labor Market: The Cyclical Vs. the Structural
items.summary: The UK labor market continues to tell two stories. The first is a cyclical downturn driven by depressed labor demand; the second is an underlying structural tightening possibly driven by problems in job matching and labor supply. That means a difficult environment for the Bank of England.

items.title: North America Hardware & Storage: Second-Quarter Preview
items.summary: Hardware OEMs’ earnings should reflect strong results given constructive commentary about infrastructure demand benefitting from AI buildouts and rising CPU usage for agentic AI workloads. Fundamentals remain strong, but expectations are also elevated. We review our preferences herein.

items.title: Global Tech Hardware: Revisiting Smartphone Forecasts
items.summary: We tweak our forecasts for global smartphone shipments in 2026 through 2028 by +5%, -5% and -4%, respectively, noting prolonged memory price strength and a higher premium model mix. Amid the downcycle of the smartphone chain, we stay selective and pick defensive players.

items.title: Equity Markets Positioning Model: Shifting Risks
items.summary: Developed-markets positioning remains constructive, but the balance of risks is shifting. New risk flows continue to underpin equity exposure, with Europe attracting some of the strongest incremental demand, while Asia is stabilizing through short covering, not outright risk addition.

items.title: Brazil Equity Strategy: Second-Quarter Earnings Wrap
items.summary: Brazil's second-quarter earnings reinforced a growing disconnect between fundamentals and share-price performance. While Ibovespa companies delivered aggregate revenue and earnings surprises of +1.8% and +5.3%, respectively, stocks fell on average after results, a dynamic explored herein.
